dossier.public_summary: A 0.6% flat-bottomed dip repeats every 1.57 days for 36 transits on a small M dwarf, with a size of about 2.9 Earth radii and no odd-even or secondary eclipses. The depth is stable in the same data product and the duration matches the star, and the difference image is consistent with the target despite being inconclusive. The best explanation is a short-period small planet, awaiting ground-based confirmation.

reasons.why: Planet-sized with flat bottom; stellar binary would be larger and typically V-shaped. Duration ratio observed_h 0.9981 vs central_h 1.023 ratio 0.9758 matches TIC radius 0.3268.

reasons.value: odd_even diff_sigma 0.6201 depth_ratio 1.1; secondary snr 2.228 best_brightening_snr 1.964 phase 0.253
reasons.why: No significant odd-even difference and no secondary eclipse above noise; rules out eclipsing binary at twice period.

reasons.value: verdict steady, p_constant_all 0.022747651977045865, QLP depth 5650 err 459, p_constant 0.05241693845326624
reasons.why: Depth steady within the main detrending product (QLP) used in 2 sectors despite input p_constant 0.02265; depth changes between products reflect calibration not astrophysical change.

reasons.why: Offset consistent with target (1.3 sigma) and only marginally with a nearby star that would need 13.15% eclipse; inconclusive location does not show off-target centroid, so planet on target remains best explanation.
